section.title: Keyboard shortcuts
section.para: On the first GTK4 run, if an old accels file exists and accels.ini does not, Geeqie asks whether to maintain the v2.x shortcuts or use the GNOME HIG shortcuts. Neither option is selected initially. Select an option to enable Continue. Canceling leaves the shortcut choice unsaved and exits; the query appears again on the next graphical launch. New installations and upgrades with an existing accels.ini are not prompted.

Restore v2.x shortcuts… replaces all keyboard shortcuts with the defaults from Geeqie v2.9 after confirmation. If the old accels file is still present in the configuration directory, its saved customizations are applied over these defaults, including disabled and alternate shortcuts. The old file is left unchanged. Commands introduced later are left unassigned. Plugin shortcuts use saved v2.x customizations when available, or the defaults supplied by the installed plugins.

The existing accels.ini is backed up as accels.ini~, replacing any previous backup. Current v3 shortcut customizations are replaced. If the old file cannot be read or converted, the current shortcuts are left unchanged. The change takes effect immediately, even if Preferences is canceled. To restore the current version's defaults, use Defaults on the Keyboard tab.

section.title: External preview extraction
section.para:
The intention of this feature is to give the user the possibility to display image previews of files that the standard libraries cannot decode.
An example is the .dng files produced by LG V30 cameras. Neither exiv2 nor libraw can extract a preview, but the command line program dcraw can.
This feature allows a work-around until the standard libraries provide a solution.
Two command files are required: one to identify which files to process, and one to extract or decode the preview image.
The format for the identification tool is:
Parameter 1: (input) full path name to the current image. Returns: 0 for file match, any other value for no match.
The format for the extraction tool is:
Parameter 1: (input) full path name to the current image. Parameter 2: (output) a temporary file name generated by Geeqie. Returns: not used.
The tool should load the output file with the decoded image.
When external previews are enabled, image and read-ahead loading waits briefly after navigation so that rapid navigation can skip intermediate files. External preview commands are serialized across image, read-ahead, and thumbnail requests. Commands for cancelled loads are terminated together with their child processes; scripts should keep their extraction work in the same process group and run it in the foreground. Missing or unreadable output is reported as a loading failure.
This is an example of an identification tool using a shell script: #! /bin/bash
filename=$(basename -- "$1") extension="${filename##*.}"
shopt -s nocasematch if [[ $extension == "DNG" ]] then cameramodel=$(exiv2 -K Exif.Image.UniqueCameraModel -Pt "$1" ) if [[ $cameramodel == "LG-H930" ]] then exit 0 else exit 1 fi else exit 1 fi
This is an example of an extraction/decode tool using a shell script: #! /bin/bash dcraw -e -c "$1" > "$2" Alternatively: #! /bin/bash gm convert "$1" "$2"
If the decode tool requires an output file with a particular extension, use this method: #! /bin/bash tmpfile=$(mktemp --tmpdir=$tempdir geeqie_tmp_XXXXXX.jpg) gm convert "$1" $tmpfile mv $tmpfile "$2"

section.title: Thread Pools
section.para: This option will limit the number of threads (cores) that are used when performing a duplicate image search. A value of 0 means use all available threads. This will give the fastest processing time, but will slow other processes including user input response time.
